notes: Account: product analytics platform used by product managers + support — conversational insights across event data.
Initial interest: move heavy inference off-hosted to Dedicated for cost predictability and lower p95 latency for interactive workflows.
POC focus: chat assistant for product insights (token-heavy), semantic search over event corpus (embeddings), and automated summarization of release notes.
Latency targets: interactive chat p95 <= 150ms desired (hard), p50 < 80ms. Throughput: sustained 200 rps for embeddings/rerank during business hours.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market — wants overall infra spend predictable; finance prefers commit + ramp vs pay-as-you-go. Asking for blended ARR with tiered discounts.
Preferred commit proposal from customer: 12-mo with staged ramp: Q1 baseline 30% commit, Q2 60%, Q3 100%; request for 25% burst capacity for seasonal spikes.
Requested pricing concessions: lower overage multiplier (1.2x vs standard 1.5x), fixed GPU-hour rate for reserved pool, cap on monthly overage bill at +40% of committed spend.
Redwood response: provided three commit buckets (small/med/large) with burst pools and suggested canary policy; offered Optimize review to tune batching and reduce unit cost.
Security: will need SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, KMS integration, and 3-year log retention for audit. Data residency: US only for now.
Legal: review open — indemnity and uptime SLA language flagged by CH legal; seeking 99.9% uptime SLA with credits spelled out.
POC acceptance criteria: Dedicated deploy passes perf tests (p95 <= 140ms, embeddings throughput >= 150 rps), integration with KMS, successful security questionnaire submission.
Quote from Head of Product: 'We need predictable bills and tail latency we can commit to — if Dedicated hits p95 targets and cost math works, we can move fast.'
Finance comment: wants monthly invoices tied to usage buckets, ability to true-up quarterly during ramp period, and clear breakout of burst vs committed consumption.
SE notes: benchmark ran on ml-gpu-rt4; observed 22% token cost reduction when moving caching + batching; still need quantization profile recommendation for 512-seq workloads.
Action items raised: Redwood to send formal SOW with explicit ramp schedule, burst definitions, overage formula, and sample monthly invoices; legal and finance to prioritize review next week.
Risks: if overage fee stays high customer may delay commit and stay on hosted (higher unit cost) — compromise needed on overage multiplier and ramp leniency.
